mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month federal funds rate over the next 60 trading days indicates a shift toward accommodative monetary policy, lowering discount rates and increasing present-value weights on future earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, the 3-month FEDFUNDS rate does not decline by at least 0.25%, or SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the 3-month federal funds rate above 5.25% triggers a tightening cycle that raises discount rates, compressing the present value of future equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05), or the 3-month FEDFUNDS rate does not remain above 5.25% for the full horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 3-month federal funds rate over the next 20 trading days signals accommodative policy, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of future earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, the 3-month FEDFUNDS rate does not decline by at least 0.1%, or SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) over the next 60 trading days indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, monthly employment growth does not rise by at least 0.5%, or SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) over the next 20 trading days signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer and business confidence and compresses earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, monthly employment growth does not fall by at least 0.3%, or SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) over the next 5 trading days indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 5-day horizon, monthly employment growth does not rise by at least 0.2%, or SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) over the next 60 trading days indicates weakening domestic manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and compresses growth expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 60-day horizon, monthly industrial production does not fall by at least 0.5%, or SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 60-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly industrial production (INDPRO) over the next 20 trading days indicates strengthening domestic manufacturing activity, which boosts corporate earnings visibility and growth expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: Over the 20-day horizon, monthly industrial production does not rise by at least 0.3%, or SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).
